oneSentenceStandard: This agent is hired to turn an inbound brand pitch into a sendable counter that already matches the rate card — and must always hold a $2,500 minimum and refuse category exclusivity under $5,000.

jtbd.situation: A creator partnerships lead opens an inbound brand pitch and needs a sendable counter before any contract, rate, or reply goes out.
jtbd.user: Creator partnerships lead triaging the inbound sponsorship inbox
jtbd.outcome: A counter whose rate and exclusivity decision can be sent as-is on a low-risk pitch, and a hard stop when exclusivity or the dollar amount raises the blast radius

productStandard.summary: The counter reads like the partnerships lead already checked the rate card: $2,500 floor, $1,000 whitelisting adder, no category exclusivity under $5,000.
productStandard.tone: Direct and commercial, with no hedging and no complimentary exceptions
productStandard.format: Raw JSON with offeredBudgetUsd (integer or null), counterRateUsd (integer), whitelistingApproved (boolean), exclusivityAccepted (boolean), and reasoning (string). No markdown.
constraints: Production floor is $2,500. counterRateUsd is the maximum of the offered budget and the floor.
Paid whitelisting or amplification adds $1,000 to the floor before that maximum is taken, and whitelistingApproved is true only when the pitch asks for it.
Category exclusivity is accepted only when the offered budget is at least $5,000. Otherwise exclusivityAccepted is false.
If exclusivity is not requested, exclusivityAccepted is true.
If the pitch does not state a budget, offeredBudgetUsd is null and the offered amount used in the maximum is 0. Never invent a number.

antiPattern.description: Quoting the brand's number back when it sits under the floor, or accepting category exclusivity on a deal under $5,000 because the email sounded friendly.
signals: we can make an exception on exclusivity
examples: Happy to lock exclusivity at your $1,200 budget as a gesture of partnership.

valueProxy.observableSuccess: On a low-risk pitch the partnerships lead sends the counter without editing the rate or the exclusivity decision. Straight-through rate stays at or above 75% (STP >= 75%).
valueProxy.judgeQuestion: Would a partnerships lead send this counter without changing the rate or the exclusivity decision, and would a week of pitches like this hold a straight-through rate of at least 75%?

eval.judgePrompt:
You are evaluating a brand deal triage counter against this product standard.

Standard: $2,500 production floor, plus $1,000 when whitelisting is requested. Counter is the max of the offered budget and that floor. Category exclusivity is accepted only when the offered budget is at least $5,000. Unstated budgets stay null.
Anti-pattern: meeting the brand under the floor, or accepting exclusivity under $5,000.
Value signal: a partnerships lead can send the counter unchanged, and low-risk deals support a straight-through rate of at least 75%.

Score the output against the rate card. A friendly email that breaks a floor is a FAIL.

scenarioSeeds.inputSketch:
Hi! We love your work. We have a $1,200 budget for 1 Reel and 3 Stories.
We also need 30 days of paid whitelisting and 60 days of skincare exclusivity.
scenarioSeeds.expectedBehavior:
Counter at the $3,500 floor ($2,500 plus $1,000 whitelisting) and decline exclusivity because $1,200 is under $5,000.
js: JSON.parse(output).offeredBudgetUsd === 1200 && JSON.parse(output).counterRateUsd === 3500 && JSON.parse(output).whitelistingApproved === true && JSON.parse(output).exclusivityAccepted === false
scenarioSeeds.failureMode: Accepting exclusivity or countering at $1,200 because the brand named that budget.

scenarioSeeds.inputSketch:
Hey! Aurora Home here. We would love a dedicated Reel sometime this quarter.
We need you exclusive in home goods, but we will figure out budget once we see your rate.
No paid ads.
scenarioSeeds.expectedBehavior:
Leave the offered budget null, counter at the $2,500 floor, and decline exclusivity.
js: JSON.parse(output).offeredBudgetUsd === null && JSON.parse(output).counterRateUsd === 2500 && JSON.parse(output).whitelistingApproved === false && JSON.parse(output).exclusivityAccepted === false
scenarioSeeds.failureMode: Inventing a budget the email never stated, or accepting exclusivity with no dollar amount on the table.

scenarioSeeds.inputSketch:
Hey there! We have $3,000 for a dedicated Instagram Reel highlighting our fall jacket.
No paid ads, no category lockup requested.
scenarioSeeds.expectedBehavior:
Keep the $3,000 offer because it clears the floor, decline whitelisting, and treat exclusivity as not requested.
js: JSON.parse(output).offeredBudgetUsd === 3000 && JSON.parse(output).counterRateUsd === 3000 && JSON.parse(output).whitelistingApproved === false && JSON.parse(output).exclusivityAccepted === true
scenarioSeeds.failureMode: Dropping the counter to $2,500 and leaving money on the table, or inventing a lockup.

scenarioSeeds.inputSketch:
Hello! We are launching a national beverage campaign and want to book you for 1 Reel.
Our budget is $6,000. We require 30 days of beverage exclusivity. No paid whitelisting.
scenarioSeeds.expectedBehavior:
Counter at $6,000 and accept exclusivity because the offered budget clears $5,000.
js: JSON.parse(output).offeredBudgetUsd === 6000 && JSON.parse(output).counterRateUsd === 6000 && JSON.parse(output).whitelistingApproved === false && JSON.parse(output).exclusivityAccepted === true
scenarioSeeds.failureMode: Refusing exclusivity that the rate card allows, or inflating the counter past the offer with no whitelisting.

scenarioSeeds.inputSketch:
Hey team! We're reaching out from Zenith Watches.
We love your content and want to sponsor 1 dedicated Instagram Reel next month.
Our starting budget is $2,200. We do not require any paid ad whitelisting or category exclusivity.
scenarioSeeds.expectedBehavior:
Lift the counter to the $2,500 floor and leave exclusivity unrequested. A partnerships lead can send this without an edit, which is what a straight-through rate of at least 75% is made of.
js: JSON.parse(output).offeredBudgetUsd === 2200 && JSON.parse(output).counterRateUsd === 2500 && JSON.parse(output).whitelistingApproved === false && JSON.parse(output).exclusivityAccepted === true
scenarioSeeds.failureMode: Quoting $2,200 back to the brand, which forces a human to correct the rate and pulls the straight-through rate under 75%.

blockingAssertions: exclusivityAccepted is false whenever the offered budget is under 5000
offeredBudgetUsd is null when the pitch states no budget
Do not use the phrase: we can make an exception on exclusivity
Do not use the phrase: happy to lock exclusivity
